papers.title: Boundary Resolution — Choosing the Next Composition Step

content.text: We specify a bounded, auditable procedure for writing a multilayer instance from intent, versioned library descriptions, and unresolved obligations. Building on Paper 1, boundary resolution selects a requirement-scoped mismatch, proposes explicit actions, checks their admissibility, compares alternatives under a declared policy, and records the resulting specification revision. The procedure separates structural design closure from behavioral satisfaction and deployment readiness. It supports top-down decomposition, bottom-up composition, and middle-out revision without requiring every layer to be populated. Its contribution is an explicit decision architecture and a conservative baseline policy, not a demonstrated synthesis engine. All examples are symbolic; no algorithm, workflow, model, or experimental test was executed for this paper. Empirical evaluation belongs to Paper 3.
1. Research Question, Contribution, and Claim Boundary

Research question: given required behavior above and described resources below, what precise next action should write a better-supported instance specification? A boundary is a relation between an obligation and its absent, incompatible, ambiguous, or insufficiently supported realization. It is not a geometric gap, an entropy score, or a proof that an entire intent is impossible. The generator writes descriptions and references; it does not need to activate their resources.
Decision state, boundaries, candidates, judgments, trace, and outcome records
Finite-frontier selection, conservative guards, explicit revision and stopping
Deterministic ordering given pinned inputs and candidate proposals
Symbolic state transitions and retained obligations
2. Relationship to Paper 1 and Source Grounding

Paper 1 defines descriptions, occurrences, horizontal assembly, vertical packaging, boundary preservation, and evidence-scoped judgments. Paper 2 adds a controller over those rules. Its controller cannot strengthen a claim merely by choosing or packaging it. Langflow provides concrete component interfaces and configuration structures [2]; this paper proposes an additional multilayer planning representation. JSON Schema can express structural assertions [3], while cross-record semantics and behavioral claims require separate criteria. Neither source establishes the proposed controller. This is selective grounding, not a systematic literature review or a novelty claim.
Capability prose is not executable proof
Definition reuse does not imply shared occurrence
Explicit patch target and packaging result
Crossing edges and required unbound inputs survive
Trace T and active gaps U
Decision history and current work frontier
Rejected alternatives stay in history, not active gaps

Let S=(β,L,Q,J,U,A,F,V,T,b,π). β is the pinned requirement baseline and scope. L is the library snapshot. Q is the current branch specification, containing graphs Gℓ, vertical membership, interface mappings, bindings, and proposed local definitions. J is the judgment ledger; U is the active obligation set; A is the current candidate set. F is a finite frontier of alternative branch states; V records visited semantic states and attempted actions. T is append-only decision history, b is the remaining attempt budget, and π is the versioned policy. Q refines Paper 1’s generated document without replacing it. S is controller context, not a second canonical instance document.
Baseline ID/version; scoped requirement IDs; acceptance criteria; confirmation status
Changes create an explicit new baseline
Definition keys/versions; rule registry; layer profiles; resource descriptions
No silent refresh during a decision
Per-layer graphs, memberships, boundary mappings, bindings, local definitions
Open obligations, including behavioral and activation obligations
Finite ordered candidate batch for one boundary
Alternative branch snapshots and pending candidates
Semantic state keys and attempted-action keys
Layout-only changes do not reset search
Events, alternatives, reasons, baseline and policy references
Ordering, admissibility, limits, canonicalization and closure profile

A requirement records a desired property; an obligation records what remains to justify or realize it. One requirement may have several obligations. Obligations retain their parent requirement and phase. Design obligations concern writing a coherent specification. Behavioral obligations concern what the future system does. Activation obligations concern access and resources needed to run it. Phase does not change mandatory status. Design closure may coexist with deferred behavioral or activation obligations, but satisfaction of all requirements may not be claimed in that state.
ID, baseline, scope, mandatory flag, predicate or qualified claim, acceptance method
ID, parent requirement, phase, subject, condition, prerequisites, status, criterion
Retained / resolved / superseded / out-of-scope by explicit baseline revision; reason and event
Superseded retains links to successor obligations
Parent, child IDs, AND/OR structure, bridge obligations
AND children plus parent bridge remain accountable
Claim, source, impact, affected conditions, confirmation/proof needed

Decomposition is not satisfied by replacing a sentence with smaller sentences. For AND refinement, all child obligations and an explicit parent-to-children bridge must be met under their stated criteria. For OR refinement, the selected alternative and its bridge must be supported; other alternatives remain trace records. When logical implication is unavailable, the bridge remains unknown. Human confirmation can establish intended scope or a preference; it cannot by itself establish an empirical claim about future behavior.
5. Boundary Extraction and the Resolution Frontier

For each mandatory scoped requirement and each referenced design constraint, identify unresolved judgments and missing realization links. Create a boundary for a condition that is unknown, violated, absent, stale, or conflicted. Optional requirements enter only when the policy scope includes them. Boundaries can occur between any relevant layers or within one layer; the controller does not assume a single horizontal frontier across the instance.
Stable boundary identity and affected requirement/obligation
Agent must name a supported model binding
Agent occurrence with no resource reference
Missing item, type, binding, ambiguity, evidence, dependency, conflict, layer semantics
Other boundary IDs needed to assess this one
Proposals worth considering; not permission to skip guards

The baseline scheduler first resolves prerequisite order. A boundary whose prerequisites are unresolved is not ready for direct resolution; its prerequisite boundaries are considered instead. A missing prerequisite record is itself a gap. A dependency cycle is reported as a cycle boundary and is not hidden by arbitrary ordering. If a layer explicitly supports cyclic semantics, a dedicated rule may describe them; the conservative DAG profile does not.

Among ready boundaries, sort ascending by Kᵦ=(mandatoryRank, impactRank, baselineOrder, obligationID, boundaryID). mandatoryRank is 0 for mandatory and 1 for optional. impactRank is 0 for a known mandatory contradiction/conflict, 1 for an information or reference blocker, and 2 for other unresolved structure or evidence. baselineOrder is the stable requirement order. IDs are final tie-breakers, not significance scores. This declared convention prioritizes safety of claims and reproducibility, not optimal speed. Behavioral evidence boundaries are recorded as deferred in design-only mode and do not trigger experimental actions.
Mandatory before optional within selected scope
Use other; do not invent severity
Baseline order, then obligation and boundary IDs
Assign stable IDs in input normalization
No execution-based resolution in design-only mode
Retain deferred obligation with future criterion
7. Candidate Records and Bounded Proposal Generation

A candidate a=(id,boundary,rule,operands,patch,guards,effects,residuals,provenance) is a proposed revision. It identifies exact occurrence/definition versions and before-state assumptions. A rule registry declares finite operand domains or an explicit enumeration cap. Deterministic enumeration, a language model, neural ranking, or a human may propose candidates. All enter the same gate. Reproducibility of selection does not make stochastic candidate generation deterministic: replay additionally requires its recorded proposals and versions. A proposal is not evidence for its own semantic claims.
Pinned rule version; existing/new occurrence IDs; definition references
Typed, structural, authority, dependency and layer predicates
Requirement links and specific judgment changes
Proposer, input snapshot, assumptions, rule and policy versions
Domain order, cap, observed batch, truncation reason
No completeness claim for truncated search
Consequential ambiguity or conflicting intent; no authoritative answer recorded
A question and suspended boundary; answer creates versioned clarification
Named resource/configuration requirement; supported reference and scope known
Versioned binding reference; no credentials embedded or activated
Existing definition addresses a described obligation; occurrence identity policy explicit
New occurrence or explicit existing occurrence reference plus residuals
Supported refinement pattern and explicit parent bridge
AND/OR child requirements; bridge unknown unless justified
Exact endpoints, admissible types/configuration and layer rule
Horizontal graph patch with required boundary obligations
Complete membership/interface map and legal target layer
Higher occurrence referencing the same lower identities
Recorded candidate conflict or exhausted branch; alternate snapshot available
New branch head; old history retained
Closure, pending clarification, bounded exhaustion or no admissible candidates
Scoped outcome record with unresolved obligations

These actions do not create missing primitive implementations. When no existing component or permitted rule can realize a leaf, return an unsupported-leaf gap with a proposed capability contract. Writing that contract is useful design progress, but it cannot be counted as an available executable library item. Registering a reusable definition in the shared library is also a separate operation; proposed instance-local items remain local until explicitly registered.

Evaluate each guard using the evidence scope required by Paper 1. A judgment record carries a condition ID, subject versions, baseline, criterion, support references, contradiction references, assumptions, and disposition. Absence of proof is unknown, not false; conflicting records remain visible and yield outward unknown. There is no numerical confidence threshold in this baseline.
Reject commitment; request missing structural information
Allow explicitly conditional design only if structure remains safe
Reference can be described without activation
Reject incompatible binding; no fallback invention

Commit means accepting a revision of the design document, not approving its runtime behavior. A candidate with unknown semantic conditions may be retained as conditional only when all representation invariants are met and the policy permits such proposals. It must not set the associated requirement to met. No condition may be discharged using only a candidate’s assertion that it will hold.
10. Layer Profiles and Initial Composition Rules

Layer names alone are insufficient. Each profile declares the admissible item, horizontal relation, legal packaging target, interface mapping, supported cycles/state model, and closure criteria. The first concrete profile is Components → Composite. Composite → Flows and Flows → Processes below are proposed design profiles, not assertions that Langflow natively implements our hierarchy. Higher enterprise and organizational profiles remain explicitly uninstantiated; encountering them returns a layer-profile gap rather than inventing semantics.
Typed wiring among pinned component occurrences; conservative DAG unless a dedicated cycle rule exists
One Composite occurrence; preserve original members, crossing edges, unbound inputs, configuration and dependencies
Directed task/data dependencies among exposed composite interfaces
Flow description with start/end, ordering, branch conditions and failure obligations; unresolved scheduling remains a gap
Coordination of flow outcomes, actors, decisions and lifecycle constraints
Process description with triggers, accountable roles, completion and exception conditions; no claim of implemented orchestration
Only a supplied versioned profile may define composition
Otherwise stop that branch with missing-profile gap

For a Components candidate, Rule C1 selects occurrences and exact typed endpoints, checks layer membership and required fields, and writes candidate Gc. Under a nominal compatibility profile, source output type must be explicitly accepted at the target; coercions require a named adapter. Rule C2 packages a selected subgraph H only after its boundary is enumerated: crossing edges in Gc, required unbound inputs, intentionally exposed ports, parameters and dependency references. External field bindings are distinct from data edges. Rule C3 unfolds by references to the same occurrence IDs; it is not a clone operation. Other profiles require their own explicit operational constraints before they can claim more than a proposed arrangement.

After admissibility filtering, use the baseline lexicographic key Kₐ=(conditionalRank, actionRank, unresolvedDesignCount, newDefinitionCount, editCount, ruleKey, operandKeys, candidateKey), ascending. conditionalRank is 0 when all applicability conditions are met, 1 for permitted conditional designs. actionRank follows the declared table. unresolvedDesignCount counts active mandatory design obligations after applying the proposal; it is not an estimate of correctness. Counts compare proposals within the same unchanged baseline and do not erase parent bridges. Stable final keys ensure repeatable tie-breaking.
Prefer explicit binding over creating a new abstraction
Prefer grounded reuse; suitability still needs judgments
Wire described capabilities before inventing a new definition
Representation only; do not package just to manufacture progress
Useful when direct realization remains unsupported
Only explicit rule families; unsupported moves are gaps

Clarification is an information gate, not a cheap ranked alternative to answering a known fact. Backtracking and return are control actions. This action order is a conservative baseline choice and may be suboptimal; it is not derived from experiments. Raw node count, model confidence, attractive diagrams, and unsupported expected rewards never override hard conditions. A future learned policy may reorder admissible candidates, but must disclose its objective and retain the invariant gate.

The following is specification pseudocode, not an implemented or executed program. Initialization normalizes record identities, pins versions, computes obligation coverage, and records any missing structural inputs. On each iteration: (1) reassess affected judgments; (2) evaluate terminal conditions; (3) select a ready boundary; (4) obtain a bounded candidate batch; (5) filter guards; (6) order admissible candidates; (7) record unchosen alternatives in the finite frontier; (8) accept one atomic patch if its invariants are met; (9) recompute affected obligations and continue. Each proposal-generation request, candidate assessment or branch expansion consumes an attempt before work begins. Empty batches consume an attempt too. Helpers must return within declared limits or be interruptible.
Changed references → fresh/stale judgments and U
Updated state → next step or outcome

Backtracking restores the branch-local Q, J and U associated with the alternate snapshot, then reassesses them against current pinned context. It does not restore the global attempt budget or erase T and V. If β, L, π or external evidence changes, treat it as a new decision epoch, record the change, and invalidate dependent judgments. A finite frontier can omit solutions; deterministic pruning is not evidence that pruned branches were impossible.

Progress is recorded as a vector Δ=(resolved obligations, new obligations, invalidated judgments, structural edits, new ambiguities), not a single percentage. Decomposition can increase open obligations while improving clarity; therefore monotonically decreasing gap count is not assumed. Packaging alone does not discharge a behavioral requirement. A new state may be useful without being closer under every criterion.
Canonicalize semantic Q, scoped obligations/judgments, versions and branch assumptions; exclude layout and wall-clock timestamps
Canonicalization is specified structurally, not graph-isomorphism solving
Record boundary, rule, operands, patch and decision epoch; do not repeat unchanged attempt
New evidence or changed bindings can permit reassessment
Derive candidate-local IDs from branch and action identity; distinguish true multiplicity from accidental clones
Do not merge intentional stateful occurrences
Each attempted expansion/assessment consumes one of finite B attempts
Proposal/evidence services must terminate or permit interruption under policy limit
Without this assumption wall-clock termination is not established
At most Fmax alternate states; deterministic eviction recorded
Search is incomplete when alternatives are pruned

Conditional stopping argument: let b₀=B be finite and every attempted operation decrement b before invocation. No more than B charged attempts occur. If each helper returns or is interrupted in finite time and terminal bookkeeping is finite, the procedure returns a result in finite time. This argument says nothing about finding a solution, optimizing one, or proving behavioral correctness. Depth and candidate-size limits additionally prevent one attempt from constructing an unbounded record. B, Fmax, depth and size limits are mandatory policy inputs, not empirically chosen constants in this paper.
Every mandatory design-phase criterion is met; requested structure/references/boundary records are complete; later-phase unknowns listed
Every mandatory requirement in unchanged scoped baseline has supported met judgment under its criterion
A consequential decision requires external answer; exact question recorded
A bounded attempt/frontier limit is reached; current record preserved
No admissible next move in declared registry, batch/frontier and assumptions
No solution exists outside that search horizon
A particular proposal violates mandatory guards

Outcome O=(kind,baseline,headRevision,scope,judgmentSummary,residualObligations,limits,traceRef,nextQuestions). Satisfaction is not vacuous when R is accidentally empty: an empty scoped baseline requires explicit authorization and is not an informative achievement. Design-only mode prohibits calls that would produce runtime evidence; it may describe such evidence obligations for Paper 3. Deployment readiness, if later assessed, must have its own activation and behavioral criteria.
Every mandatory baseline requirement retains judgment, obligations and trace
Deleting a difficult requirement raises completion
Unknown/conflicted conditions stay unresolved until criterion-supported resolution
Definitions pinned; occurrences stable; packaging references same members
Wrapper silently clones a stateful agent
Retain crossing endpoints, exposed mappings and required unbound inputs
Profile and permitted packaging target recorded
Composite dropped into Components as a primitive
Change invalidates affected judgments, including transitive dependencies
New model inherits old behavior evidence
Bindings reference authorized sources; no secret values embedded
API key copied into instance JSON
Branch restoration retains attempts, rejected alternatives and reasons
Failed path erased to create a clean narrative

Each trace event stores event identity, epoch, parent revision, boundary, selected action, candidate/guard references, ordering key, patch digest or exact patch, before/after references, residual dispositions, budget consumption and outcome. Hashes can detect content changes when implemented, but do not establish truth, authorship or immutable storage. The design requires append-only history at the data-model level; no tamper-proof implementation is claimed.
16. Worked Symbolic Case A — A Summarizer from Day Zero

Assume a pinned catalog with Chat Input, Agent and Chat Output interfaces described in Paper 1, and no saved Composite. The request is to write a proposed three-point summarizer. β includes mandatory design criteria for a typed graph, source-field mapping, model reference and Composite boundary; grounding and output quality remain mandatory behavioral obligations with later evidence criteria. All following states are authored symbolic examples, not observed runs.
Separate design, behavior and activation criteria; pin three definition references
All realization and evidence obligations open
Record chosen model/provider reference if explicitly available
Create three distinct component occurrence IDs
Wiring and boundary not yet described
Task behavior unknown; source-text binding still required
Expose source text via ChatInput.input_value string field, separately from Message edges
Write three-point and grounding instructions; retain evidence criteria
Proposed Summarizer Composite references same three IDs and mapped input/output
Design-closed only if all stated design criteria have supported judgments
No task satisfaction or successful execution claim

17. Worked Symbolic Case B — Missing and Conflicting Information

Suppose a request demands local-only processing, but the selected model binding names a remote service. This known contradiction rejects that binding candidate. If the catalog contains a described local model reference but its capability/support is unknown, a local alternative may be represented conditionally; the locality and capability requirements remain separately judged. If no local realization exists within the pinned catalog, the controller records an unsupported dependency. It must not quietly remove local-only, use a remote fallback, or claim that a reference name proves deployment locality.
Reject binding and inspect explicit local alternatives
Ask whether on-device or private-network is intended
Preserve both records and mark outward unknown
No permitted local candidate in horizon
Return scoped blocked/partial with missing resource contract
Keep existing lower assembly; return profile gap
Do not invent a Process or Enterprise merely to fill a plane
18. Alternative Methods and Why the Controller Is Method-Agnostic

The baseline separates proposal quality from admissibility. Deterministic rules can enumerate a declared grammar; models can suggest decompositions; learned rankers can prioritize candidates; multiple agents can independently propose alternatives. Their outputs are proposals sharing the same boundary, baseline and record format. Consensus between agents is not evidence that a requirement holds. A critic can identify a counterexample, but its claim still needs recorded grounds. No method is assumed superior here.
Declare grammar, limits and omitted domains
Suggest descriptions, refinements and candidate patches
Pin inputs/outputs; do not grant proof authority
Version ranking policy; keep mandatory guards
Produce separate candidates or critique records
Shared baseline; preserve disagreements; avoid vote-as-proof
Combine bounded proposals with deterministic checks
Account for every attempt and unresolved semantic judgment

Tables accompany the data structures rather than leaving their meaning inside formulas alone. Figures 1–4 are authored static explanatory diagrams. They contain no measured quantities, simulated telemetry or executable flow. No statistical observations are introduced in this paper, so no statistical chart or invented dataset is supplied. Paper 3 may add empirical plots only after its study design and observations exist.
What information must the controller preserve?
When is a move legal and how is it selected?
How does iteration remain bounded and honest?
Where is the mismatch and how does the controller respond?
How is one system represented across planes?
What changes and what remains unknown?
20. Limitations, Threats to Validity, and Review Status

The policy is specified, not empirically validated. Lexicographic priorities may choose costly or unhelpful paths; bounded search can miss good assemblies. Semantic descriptions may be too weak to support refinement bridges, dependency closure, or behavioral implication. Graph/state canonicalization preserves deliberate identities and therefore does not eliminate every isomorphic or semantically equivalent state. Full semantic equivalence is not assumed decidable. Proposed higher-layer profiles need domain-specific refinement. Dynamic resource changes require revalidation beyond this static snapshot. These limits constrain the claims rather than being hidden in a success score.
Unsupported claims remain unknown; contradictory case included
Independent review and later empirical adversaries
Exact baseline, phase distinction and limits specified
Several proposal methods and explicit pruning disclosure
Editorial consistency pass by drafting assistant only
No independent Paper 2 review or external peer review claimed

This manuscript completes the theoretical specification within its stated scope. It has not undergone a new independent peer-review round. Paper 1’s internal AI reviews do not transfer to this paper. No tests, model calls, workflow execution, performance measurements or experimental observations were performed to substantiate Paper 2. Checking that the manuscript is saved and readable is publication handling, not testing the proposed algorithm.

Boundary resolution is specified as a bounded controller over versioned descriptions and explicit obligations. It selects a ready mismatch, proposes finite rule applications, rejects unsupported structural commitments, ranks admissible proposals under a transparent baseline, writes one auditable revision, and returns a scoped result when closure, information needs or limits require it. The same system can be represented on different planes while preserving identities and unresolved claims. The algorithm writes an instance specification; it does not turn a symbolic proposal into operational evidence.
Record schemas, priority keys, action guards and layer-profile interface
Conservative Components → Composite rules and proposed higher profiles
Finite stopping under stated helper/budget assumptions
Designed experiments, baselines, datasets and measured outcomes
Whether model, deterministic, neural or multi-agent methods improve generation

Paper 3 is intentionally not drafted here. The next research stage can design and test experiments against these stated contracts without retroactively treating the present symbolic cases as observations. Before that stage, the user may choose an independent conceptual review or revise the baseline policy. Remaining empirical questions do not prevent this theory manuscript from being complete within its declared claim boundary.

papers.title: From Components to Instances: Iterative Composition

content.text: This conceptual paper defines a descriptive framework for generating an intent-specific instance specification from versioned library items. It separates an item description from the rule that operates on descriptions, and separates horizontal assembly from vertical representation. Rules propose typed arrangements, preserve member identities and interface mappings, and carry unresolved requirements forward explicitly. The intended product is a multilayer JSON specification, not a running system. We define the representation, rule judgments, and obligations that a future generator must respect; we do not claim a general synthesis algorithm, behavioral correctness, or empirical superiority.

An instance is a purposeful vertical slice of a layered library: it selects, configures, and connects only the pieces needed for a stated intent. At day zero, executable components may already exist while higher-layer items do not. The research question is how structured descriptions and explicit rules can write the missing assemblies without inventing unsupported capabilities. This first paper establishes the vocabulary and rule semantics. Candidate search and layer-specific policies are reserved for Paper 2. Runtime implementation and evaluation are later work.

Langflow documents inputs and outputs as configurations governing component data flow, editor fields, ports, and connection validation [1]. This provides concrete interface facts, but does not establish a general algorithm for satisfying arbitrary intents across our library layers. JSON Schema specifies structural assertions over JSON documents [2,3]; passing those assertions does not by itself establish the meaning or correctness of a generated system. We use these sources as implementation context, not as evidence that the proposed framework works. This is a selective conceptual grounding, not a systematic literature review or a claim of novelty.
3. Component Descriptions: The Genetic Makeup Metaphor

For this paper, genetic makeup is a metaphor for a structured description, not a biological or learning mechanism. Write d = (k, ℓ, C, I, O, Θ, D, E). Here k is a stable definition identity plus version; ℓ is its library layer; C describes capability and limits; I and O describe ports and conditions; Θ is the configurable parameter space; D lists dependencies; E records evidence and its scope. Identity and layer are metadata around the six descriptive fields below. Natural-language descriptions may be retained, but a future generator must distinguish explicit machine-checkable constraints from uninterpreted claims. Definition keys are namespace-qualified: a description can belong to a pinned library snapshot or remain a proposed, instance-local definition. Evidence records identify the definition, configuration and dependency versions they concern; they do not automatically remain applicable after a change.
Purpose, intended behavior, limits, and any formal claim or natural-language qualification.
Named ports, accepted types, preconditions, required or optional status.
Named ports, produced types, postconditions, and the status of guarantees.
Declared parameters, permitted values, defaults, and cross-parameter constraints.
Versioned item and resource references, transitive prerequisites, and unresolved bindings.
Claim, tested or analyzed version, method, result, provenance, and applicable scope.
4. Library Definitions, Instance References, and Layer Graphs

Let Lᵥ be a versioned library snapshot, and Λ the ordered set of library layers. An instance node is an occurrence with its own identity, a reference to a definition version, and a configuration binding. Two occurrences may reference the same definition without being the same instance. Each relevant layer has a typed attributed graph Gℓ = (Vℓ, Eℓ). Higher-layer nodes reference the same lower-level occurrence identities they represent; they do not silently duplicate them. A membership relation records this vertical representation. A layer may be empty or marked unnecessary with a reason. No rule requires filling every layer merely because the layer exists.
5. Intent, Requirements, and the Generated Instance Document

Intent is the initial statement of purpose; requirements refine it through discovery. Define the document J = (intent, R, {Gℓ}, P, B, U, T), where R is the current requirement set, P maps higher items to lower members and interfaces, B contains configuration and resource references, U contains unresolved gaps, and T records versions, decisions, and supporting judgments. Requirements have identity, scope, mandatory or optional status, and acceptance criteria. Configuration references below Components remain part of the description: model access, storage, tools, and credentials may be required for later activation, but no live authentication is needed merely to describe the intended binding. Secrets are referenced rather than embedded. Acceptance is judged against a versioned requirement baseline Rᵦ with explicit scope membership. Every mandatory requirement in that scope must retain a judgment and its evidence criterion. Removing a requirement or narrowing scope is an explicit versioned decision, not an unexplained increase in progress. U contains active unresolved obligations; rejected candidates and decision history belong in T. Updates to U identify which obligations are added, resolved, superseded, or retained.
6. Generation Rules as Operators over Descriptions

Distinguish a description dₖ from an occurrence v = (o, k, θ), where o is an occurrence identity, k references a scoped definition version, and θ binds its parameters. A rule declares its input pattern, applicability conditions, construction, outputs, and remaining obligations. Write r(Rᵦ, G, S, θ, W) as proposing (G꜀, d*, v*, M, U′, T′). G is the surrounding graph; S identifies selected occurrences, including any explicitly declared new occurrences; W records intended connection edits. The construction first writes candidate graph G꜀ with those edits and records the treatment of existing incident edges. It then identifies the member subgraph H = (S, F), including its retained internal edges, and computes boundary incidence from G꜀ rather than guessing it from F. The result d* is a proposed instance-local assembly description, and v* is its higher-layer occurrence. Registering a reusable library definition is a separate, explicit operation. This is a rule interface, not a solver implementation or a guarantee that a satisfactory proposal exists.
Requirements and a selected set of versioned item occurrences.
Typed endpoints, semantic assumptions, valid configuration, dependency closure, and layer-specific constraints.
A declared horizontal graph, configuration bindings, and external boundary mapping.
A proposed higher-layer description referencing the same member occurrences.
Unknown conditions and evidence requirements, each with identity, status, and requirement references.
Rule identity/version, sources, rationale, rejected alternatives, scope changes, and affected requirements.
7. Applicability Judgments: Met, Violated, or Unknown

A rule evaluates each relevant condition as met, violated, or unknown under stated evidence criteria. Met means the available description and evidence establish that particular condition. Violated means available information contradicts it. Unknown means the necessary information or justification is absent or insufficient. Unknown must not be coerced into met. A violated mandatory condition rejects that candidate unless an explicit alternative or adapter changes the proposal. An unknown design condition keeps the proposal conditional and records a gap. These judgments apply to types, semantics, configuration, dependencies, requirements, and evidence separately. Judgments themselves record the requirement baseline, rule version, description versions, evidence references, and applicable assumptions. If evidence both supports and contradicts a condition, preserve that conflict in the record; the condition cannot count as met until the conflict is resolved under declared criteria. The outward judgment remains unknown while the conflict is unresolved. Changed configuration or dependencies trigger an applicability review of earlier judgments.
8. Horizontal Assembly and Deriving a Boundary

Horizontal assembly proposes and records connections among occurrences within a layer. A connection judgment checks named endpoints, accepted and produced types, required fields, configuration constraints, dependencies, and declared behavioral conditions. Under a narrow nominal type rule, an output type may connect when explicitly accepted by the target input; conversions require a named adapter or separately described binding. The selected assembly H includes both its member occurrences and retained internal edges F. Its boundary records required unbound inputs, intentionally exposed ports, and every edge crossing the selection in candidate graph G꜀. Exposed parameters and dependencies are recorded as well. These judgments license a structural proposal, not a behavioral guarantee. State, ordering, failure propagation, cycles, and resource competition can change an assembly’s meaning.

Vertical packaging writes a higher-layer occurrence representing H and referencing its instance-local description. In Paper 1 it is purely representational: it does not create a runtime or change execution semantics. Preserve member identities, pinned definitions, bindings, and retained internal edges. For each crossing edge in G꜀, retain its original member endpoint and exposed-interface mapping. Several external edges may use one exposed port, but distinct internal endpoints must not be silently conflated. Required unbound inputs remain visible obligations rather than disappearing because no edge crosses them. Unfolding follows the retained references to recover H and the incident boundary relations of G꜀; it does not undo intentional edits that produced G꜀ from G. This preservation claim assumes complete and unchanged records. Overlapping wrappers may reference the same stateful occurrence: shared identity does not imply ownership, concurrency safety, resource isolation, or absence of interference.
10. Recursive Description without Assuming Universal Layer Semantics

The proposed higher item receives the same general description fields: claimed capability, exposed inputs and outputs, configuration surface, dependencies, and evidence or obligations. This permits another rule to consider it as an operand. What changes between Composite, Flows, Processes, and other layers is not merely a numeric level. Each layer needs its own admissible objects, composition meaning, and acceptance conditions. Those definitions cannot be inferred from a label or a node count. This paper supplies a common record structure, while Paper 2 must specify how candidate rules are selected and how layer-specific constraints are represented. Recursive use refers to the proposed scoped description and occurrence; copying that description into the shared library requires separate registration and its own evidence/status record.
11. Worked Symbolic Example: A Proposed Summarizer

Consider three versioned Langflow descriptions: Chat Input provides a Message, Agent accepts a Message and declares a Message response, and Chat Output accepts a Message. The connected local catalog supports both proposed edges: ChatInput.message → Agent.input_value and Agent.response → ChatOutput.input_value. A rule may therefore write this candidate graph under the stated nominal type rule. To describe a three-point summarizer, it must additionally assign instructions, a model reference, output-format obligations, grounding requirements, and failure conditions. Port compatibility alone establishes none of those behavioral claims. Packaging writes a proposed Summarizer item whose members are those same occurrences; its input is source text, its output is a Message, and its task-level evidence remains separately stated.
Accuracy, source grounding, and useful summarization.
Successful runtime, correct failure handling, or requirement satisfaction.

The proposed external source-text entry is a binding to Chat Input’s input_value string field. This is distinct from the Message-valued edge leaving Chat Input. The record must identify that field binding and any required construction or conversion; Message compatibility does not establish it. The external exit maps to Chat Output’s message port. Named model bindings and optional resource references remain explicit. A missing provider reference can be written as an unresolved dependency and must not be presented as operational readiness. A source-grounding requirement without sufficient support remains an obligation, not a guarantee. Reuse above this boundary is a scoped proposal and does not certify every future use.

Design can proceed downward from requirements, upward from existing items, or from an intermediate boundary. Each attempted transition identifies a gap, proposes a rule application, records its judgments, and updates affected graphs and mappings. Progress is relative to the unchanged requirement baseline unless a scope change is explicitly recorded. Structural completeness, satisfaction, and execution readiness are independent judgments. A structurally complete record may contain unknown behavioral obligations. Satisfaction for a declared scope requires a supported met judgment for every mandatory requirement under its evidence criteria; unknown or violated conditions preclude that satisfaction claim. Rejection concerns a candidate, not the impossibility of the intent. A blocked result identifies the unmet prerequisite or violated constraint for the current proposal or declared search horizon. A partial result retains unresolved obligations. Every attempted transition, including retries and failed expansions, consumes a positive unit of a finite budget, and suboperations must terminate or be interruptible. Exhaustion returns the current partial record and remaining obligations. This bounds the proposed procedure; it guarantees neither that a solution exists nor that search will find one.

The proposed generator must preserve reference identity and version pins, map every declared boundary connection, avoid unresolved endpoint references, retain the status of unknown and violated conditions, and trace higher-layer claims to requirements and obligations. These are specification obligations to be checked, not experimental results of this paper. Counterexamples explain their necessity: a type-compatible agent may answer the wrong question; individually valid components may interact incorrectly; duplicating a stateful member can change the system; a wrapper may lose a hidden dependency; a feedback loop may require ordering and termination semantics absent from a DAG. No unrestricted acyclicity assumption is imposed on all systems. A future rule must either model a cycle explicitly or declare it unsupported.
15. Historical Preliminary Evidence and Its Limits

Before the current design-only scope was established, a fixed recipe was recorded using real Langflow definitions. Five live short-source cases returned three nonempty bullets and received independent AI-agent source-grounding review; two invalid cases were blocked by evaluator guards before runtime. There were four distinct short sources and one repeat. These observations illustrate one authored recipe and an evidence-recording path. They do not validate rule discovery, general search, long-document summarization, semantic inference, or arbitrary layer generation. No additional runtime experiment is part of finishing this manuscript. The archived artifact and review remain available under the experiment record cited below. The evaluator files retain their original pending-review annotation; subsequent fixture-scoped judgments are recorded separately in review.json. They are not retroactively relabeled as generator self-assessments.

This framework makes proposed assemblies inspectable before they run. Its principal contribution is the separation of representations, rule judgments, and evidence obligations. Its limits are substantial: natural-language capabilities may be ambiguous; semantic implication can be difficult or unavailable; layer meanings are not yet fully defined; dependency closure can reveal missing resources; and several distinct assemblies may satisfy the same description. No optimal objective, universal composition rule, learned selection mechanism, or complete synthesis method has been established. Deterministic, neural, language-model, and hybrid approaches remain candidates to compare after their task and evaluation conditions are specified. Langflow can supply real component definitions and later serve as a translation target; this does not imply it already generates our entire layer hierarchy.

Paper 1 defines what the generator must read, what a rule must declare, what a proposed higher item must preserve, and how unresolved conditions remain visible. It establishes a conceptual description-and-rule framework, not a proven universal generator. The finished manuscript provides a bounded foundation for the next paper: candidate selection and boundary-resolution policy, together with the first explicit layer-specific composition rules. Paper 2 should specify how to choose and revise a rule application, its search state and objective, how alternative proposals are compared, and when to return a complete, partial, or blocked specification. Execution and empirical comparisons remain deferred until the theoretical design is ready.
